key_insight: TRACE-ROUTER reframes model routing for agentic AI as a task-level, delayed-feedback problem instead of making isolated per-call decisions. It aims to learn routing policies that stay consistent with the overall workflow outcome, not just the immediate call.
problem_solved: Current LLM routers choose models independently for each request, which works poorly for agentic workflows where success is only visible at the end of a long sequence of actions. This creates a credit-assignment problem: the router cannot tell which individual routing choices helped or hurt the final task result.
method: Uses online routing that adapts during execution of agentic workflows rather than relying only on static or per-call decisions.
Introduces task-consistent routing logic so model selection is optimized for delayed, end-to-end task success.
Accounts for the long-horizon nature of agent workflows by attributing feedback across multiple routing decisions.
impact: For practitioners deploying LLM agents, this could improve quality-cost trade-offs by choosing cheaper or stronger models more intelligently over the course of a task. It is especially relevant for enterprise systems where reliability, latency, and budget must be balanced across multi-step workflows.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing a multi-step agent pipeline with routing decisions at each step and a final task outcome
Comparison graphic of per-call routing versus task-consistent routing
Credit-assignment timeline illustrating delayed feedback from the final result back to earlier routing choices
Trade-off chart mapping model cost against quality with adaptive routing paths
paper_title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
paper_authors: Ritik Raj, Souvik Kundu, Sarbartha Banerjee, Dheemanth Joshi, Ishita Vohra
